cards.title: Nouns: quick review
cards.body: Common (city) vs proper (Chicago, with a capital). Concrete (drum), abstract (courage), collective (team). Plurals: -s, -es, -ies, -ves, and irregulars (children, feet, mice). Possessives: one owner ’s (the dog’s), plural owners s’ (the dogs’), irregular plurals ’s (the children’s).

cards.title: Pronouns: quick review
cards.body: Subject: I, he, she, we, they (doing the action). Object: me, him, her, us, them (receiving it, or after with/to/for/between). Possessive: my/mine, our/ours, their/theirs — never an apostrophe. Agreement: one → it/its, many → they/their. Clear: use a name when a pronoun could mean two people.

cards.title: How the check works
cards.body: First, a 10-question quiz: you need 8 right (80%) to pass. If you don’t pass, you’ll see which skills to review, and you’ll get new questions next time. Then you’ll write a short paragraph that shows off everything you’ve learned. Quill gives it a score.

prompts: What did you learn about nouns or pronouns that you didn’t know before this unit?
